The service then runs `safeParse` and sets `this.options = null` on validation failure. A caller providing `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without `teamId` will now pass the TypeScript type check but fail validation at runtime, causing the service to silently return `NOTHING_CONDITION` for every query. This is a type safety regression that can hide authorization errors and prevent access without any error message."

However, the service builds `teamIds` from `teamRepo.findAllByParentId()` which does not specify an `orderBy`, and the test data is created without any guaranteed ordering. The database may return teams in any order, making the test flaky. The same issue applies to the array of user IDs, which comes from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds()` without an explicit order. findings.title: Removal of public findMany method breaks existing callers
findings.body: The public `findMany` method has been removed and replaced with `getBaseConditions`. Any code that previously called `service.findMany(...)` will now fail to compile or break at runtime. This is an API contract break that will affect any consumers of this service (e.g., API route handlers) that were not updated in this PR. The maintainer should either retain the method or update all callers before merging.

findings.title: Constructor accepts looser public options type leading to silent validation failures
findings.body: The constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` (the strict z.infer type) to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, which makes `teamId` optional for all scopes. The service then runs `safeParse` and sets `this.options = null` on validation failure. A caller providing `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without `teamId` will now pass the TypeScript type check but fail validation at runtime, causing the service to silently return `NOTHING_CONDITION` for every query. This is a type safety regression that can hide authorization errors and prevent access without any error message.

findings.title: Integration test relies on unspecified ordering of database query results
findings.body: The org scope test expects the `Prisma.sql` condition to contain the array `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` in that exact order. However, the service builds `teamIds` from `teamRepo.findAllByParentId()` which does not specify an `orderBy`, and the test data is created without any guaranteed ordering. The database may return teams in any order, making the test flaky. The same issue applies to the array of user IDs, which comes from `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds()` without an explicit order. The tests should either sort the expected arrays or the service should sort the results before building the SQL.

findings.title: Integration test may fail due to asynchronous denormalized table updates
findings.body: The `getBaseConditions` test now uses `prisma.$queryRaw` to query the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table immediately after creating bookings. If this table is populated asynchronously (e.g., by a background job or materialized view refresh), the newly created `userBooking` may not be present when the query runs, causing the test to fail. The PR description itself notes that the test runner could not be executed, leaving this risk unverified. A more robust test would wait for the denormalized table to be updated or mock the underlying data source.

findings.title: Caching tests were removed, leaving caching behavior untested
findings.body: The PR removes the entire `Caching` describe block that verified authorization and filter conditions are cached. The service still implements caching via `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, so this behavior is no longer covered by tests. If the caching logic is faulty (e.g., stale data or incorrect invalidation), it could go undetected. A low-effort fix is to reintroduce tests that assert the same object is returned on repeated calls.
